summary.headline: 1000000211: estimated recovery below the cost of a demand
summary.rationale: 1000000211 billed 99215 on 7.1% of 622 claims against an expected 3.9% given patient complexity (risk-adjusted score 1.60; plain z-score vs peers 0.13). 59% of this provider's 99215 claims were on patients with 0 or 1 chronic conditions. Records came back for 43 claims. Of 5 documented 99215 claims, 2 (40%) were documented below the billed level, against 42% for the comparison providers. Note checks on 30 returned notes (share showing each sign): problems 53%, late 3%, unsigned 0%, data 3%. No audit trail was received. 3 of 29 notes claiming moderate-or-higher data reviewed had no lab or test line on the claim. This pattern is consistent with upcoding. It is a reason to review the records, not a finding. Examples: C0091898: billed 99215, patient aged 56 with 0 chronic condition(s); documented MDM level moderate, 33 minutes. C0091903: billed 99215, patient aged 18 with 0 chronic condition(s); documented MDM level low, 29 minutes. C0091759: billed 99215, patient aged 27 with 0 chronic condition(s). C0091788: billed 99215, patient aged 81 with 0 chronic condition(s). C0091858: billed 99215, patient aged 55 with 1 chronic condition(s) (hypertension); documented MDM level high, minutes not recorded. No demand is sent: the estimated recovery (lower bound $0) is below the staff cost of a demand ($276).
next_steps: Request the full charts for C0091898, C0091903, C0091759 and have a certified coder re-score each against the current E/M rules (medical decision making or total time).
If the re-scoring confirms the pattern, review the random sample in the recovery packet's sampling plan before any overpayment estimate; do not extrapolate from a targeted sample.
Look at the notes themselves: 53% address fewer problems than their level implies and 3% were signed late; request the audit trail for C0091898, C0091903, C0091759.

summary.headline: Office objected, then did not respond; no charts
summary.rationale: 1000000178 billed 99215 on 6.2% of 773 claims against an expected 5.5% given patient complexity (risk-adjusted score 0.29; plain z-score vs peers -0.05). 23% of this provider's 99215 claims were on patients with 0 or 1 chronic conditions. Records came back for 0 claims. No documented 99215 claims came back. Claims show only a modest excess (1.13x expected). The office sent no usable charts after one follow-up. Non-response is not evidence of upcoding. Examples: C0075679: billed 99215, patient aged 36 with 0 chronic condition(s). C0075745: billed 99215, patient aged 49 with 1 chronic condition(s) (obesity).
next_steps: No usable charts yet: request a random sample of 30 charts, then a targeted sample of 99215s for C0075679, C0075745.
If the practice does not respond, record that non-response is not evidence of upcoding and decide whether the claims signal alone warrants more.
